statements.t: We estimate that we incurred costs before mitigation actions from the 2025 incremental tariff rates of approximately $50 million in 2025, and we implemented various actions to fully offset the effect of the current incremental tariffs in 2026.
We distributed $3 million in refunds to our customers during the three months ended September 30, 2026, and we anticipate distributing additional refunds during the fourth quarter of 2026.
In April 2026, the U.S. government also issued an update to the definition of Section 232 tariffs, which is not expected to have a significant effect on our ongoing tariff obligations.
The provision for taxes is based upon our projected annual effective tax rate of 19.0% before non-recurring discrete tax items for the periods ended September 30, 2026 and 2025.
difference between our projected annual effective tax rate and the reported tax rate is related to the timing of excess tax benefits associated with stock option exercises.

We expect, but are not obligated, to terminate the plan and subsequently enter into a buy-out agreement to transfer responsibility for future benefit payments to an insurance company in 2027, subject to regulatory approvals and customary administrative procedures.
We do not anticipate making a significant employer contribution to the plan related to the termination.
Upon completion of the buy-out, we expect to recognize a one-time non-cash charge in net earnings related to the deferred actuarial loss included in accumulated other comprehensive income.

We will receive proceeds of approximately $31 million, of which approximately $18 million is expected to offset future purchases of property, plant, and equipment and approximately $13 million is expected to offset future operating expenses.
We expect to receive proceeds and make payments related to the agreement through 2030.

Based on our outstanding debt at September 30, 2026, we estimate that a 5% weakening of the U.S. dollar against the currencies in which our debt is denominated would result in an increase of approximately $51.9 million in the reported U.S. dollar value of our debt.

statements.t: Based on today's assessment, management anticipates local currency sales for the fourth quarter of 2026 will increase approximately 5%.
For the full year 2026, management anticipates local currency sales will increase approximately 5%, which excludes the impact of tariff refunds to customers.
The Company stated that based on its assessment of market conditions today, management anticipates local currency sales growth of approximately 5% in 2027.
As market conditions improve, we are well positioned to deliver strong financial performance going forward.”
